claims.text: Maximum margin methods such as boosted trees and boosted stumps push probability mass away from 0 and 1.
Maximum margin methods produce a characteristic sigmoid-shaped distortion in predicted probabilities.
Naive Bayes models push predicted probabilities toward 0 and 1.
Neural networks predict well-calibrated probabilities without systematic probability mass distortion.
Bagged trees predict well-calibrated probabilities without systematic probability mass distortion.
After calibration, boosted trees predict the best probabilities among tested models.
After calibration, random forests predict the best probabilities among tested models.
After calibration, support vector machines predict the best probabilities among tested models.

methodologies.name: Platt Scaling
methodologies.description: A parametric transformation method used to calibrate predicted probabilities by fitting a logistic regression model on model outputs.

methodologies.name: Isotonic Regression
methodologies.description: A non-parametric calibration method that fits a non-decreasing monotonic function to map predicted outputs to true posteriors.

limitations.text: Naive Bayes relies on unrealistic attribute independence assumptions, causing systematic probability distortions.
